This week introduces **probability distributions**: random variables, the p/d/q/r function family in R, and the Binomial, Negative Binomial, Poisson, Normal and t-distributions — plus how they relate to each other. Use the language toggle above to switch between R and Python.

<h3>Quiz 1: Distribution Functions in R <span id="quiz-done-w5_q_functions" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> R's distribution functions share a root name prefixed by <code>p</code>, <code>d</code>, <code>q</code> or <code>r</code> (e.g. <code>pnorm</code>, <code>dnorm</code>, <code>qnorm</code>, <code>rnorm</code>). What does the <code>q</code>-prefix stand for?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fn1" id="fn1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="fn1a">Quality of fit</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fn1" id="fn1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="fn1b">Quantile — the inverse of the cumulative distribution function</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fn1" id="fn1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="fn1c">Quick random draw</label></div>
    <div id="fn1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> What does <code>pnorm(1.9, mean=1.75, sd=0.15, lower.tail=FALSE)</code> compute?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fn2" id="fn2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="fn2a">The probability of a value being greater than 1.9</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fn2" id="fn2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="fn2b">The probability of a value being less than 1.9</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fn2" id="fn2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="fn2c">A random sample from the distribution</label></div>
    <div id="fn2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> What does <code>qnorm(c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), mean=2, sd=1)</code> return?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fn3" id="fn3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="fn3a">The cumulative probabilities at x = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fn3" id="fn3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="fn3b">The x-values corresponding to the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles of that normal distribution</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="fn3" id="fn3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="fn3c">Three random draws from the distribution</label></div>
    <div id="fn3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkFunctionsQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="functions-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 2: Binomial &amp; Negative Binomial <span id="quiz-done-w5_q_binomial" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> What does <code>dbinom(5, size=5, prob=0.5)</code> compute?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="bn1" id="bn1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="bn1a">The probability of getting exactly 5 successes out of 5 trials</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="bn1" id="bn1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="bn1b">The probability of getting 5 or fewer successes out of 5 trials</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="bn1" id="bn1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="bn1c">The expected number of successes</label></div>
    <div id="bn1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> A footballer scores 90% of penalties (p = 0.9) and takes 20 in training (L = 20). Using <code>E(X) = L·p</code>, the expected number of goals is 18. What do <code>L</code> and <code>p</code> represent in the binomial distribution?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="bn2" id="bn2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="bn2a"><code>L</code> = number of independent trials, <code>p</code> = probability of success on each trial</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="bn2" id="bn2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="bn2b"><code>L</code> = number of successes, <code>p</code> = number of trials</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="bn2" id="bn2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="bn2c"><code>L</code> and <code>p</code> are interchangeable</label></div>
    <div id="bn2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> What does the negative binomial distribution describe?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="bn3" id="bn3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="bn3a">The probability of exactly k successes in a fixed number of trials</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="bn3" id="bn3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="bn3b">The number of failures (or trials) needed to reach a fixed number of successes <code>r</code></label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="bn3" id="bn3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="bn3c">The probability that a continuous variable falls below a threshold</label></div>
    <div id="bn3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkBinomialQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="binomial-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 3: Poisson Distribution <span id="quiz-done-w5_q_poisson" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> The Poisson distribution has a single parameter λ, with <code>E(X) = Var(X) = λ</code>. In the gene mutation example, what did λ represent?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ps1" id="ps1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="ps1a">The probability of any single mutation occurring</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ps1" id="ps1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="ps1b">The average (expected) number of mutations accumulated after one generation</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ps1" id="ps1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="ps1c">The total number of genes in the genome</label></div>
    <div id="ps1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> What does <code>ppois(q = 10, lambda = 30)</code> compute?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ps2" id="ps2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="ps2a">The probability of observing exactly 10 events</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ps2" id="ps2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="ps2b">The probability of observing 10 or fewer events, given an average rate of 30</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ps2" id="ps2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="ps2c">A random draw from a Poisson distribution</label></div>
    <div id="ps2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> On average 50 students attend a lecture. Which function computes the probability that <em>exactly</em> 60 students show up?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ps3" id="ps3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="ps3a"><code>dpois(60, lambda = 50)</code></label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ps3" id="ps3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="ps3b"><code>ppois(60, lambda = 50)</code></label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="ps3" id="ps3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="ps3c"><code>rpois(60, lambda = 50)</code></label></div>
    <div id="ps3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkPoissonQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="poisson-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 4: Normal &amp; t-Distribution <span id="quiz-done-w5_q_normal" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> In the TP53 gene expression example, why can we use the sample mean and standard deviation from 586 patients as <code>mu</code> and <code>sigma</code> of a normal distribution model?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nt1" id="nt1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="nt1a">Because we cannot measure every lung cancer patient in the world, so the sample statistics estimate the population parameters</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nt1" id="nt1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="nt1b">Because R requires exactly 586 data points for <code>dnorm()</code></label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nt1" id="nt1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="nt1c">Because normal distributions only work with gene expression data</label></div>
    <div id="nt1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> What makes the <strong>standard</strong> normal distribution special?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nt2" id="nt2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="nt2a">It has mean = 0 and standard deviation = 1</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nt2" id="nt2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="nt2b">It only applies to sample sizes below 30</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nt2" id="nt2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="nt2c">It has no variance</label></div>
    <div id="nt2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> What happens to the t-distribution as the degrees of freedom increase?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nt3" id="nt3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="nt3a">Its tails get wider and wider</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nt3" id="nt3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="nt3b">It converges towards the standard normal distribution</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="nt3" id="nt3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="nt3c">It becomes a Poisson distribution</label></div>
    <div id="nt3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkNormalQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="normal-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>

<hr>

<h3>Quiz 5: Relationships Between Distributions (Plenum) <span id="quiz-done-w5_q_relationships" class="quiz-done-badge">✓ Done</span></h3>
<div class="quiz-card">
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 1:</strong> Under what condition does the Poisson distribution become approximately equivalent to a Normal distribution?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="rl1" id="rl1a"><label class="form-check-label" for="rl1a">When λ is large (λ ≫ 1)</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="rl1" id="rl1b"><label class="form-check-label" for="rl1b">When λ = 0</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="rl1" id="rl1c"><label class="form-check-label" for="rl1c">Only for discrete data</label></div>
    <div id="rl1-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 2:</strong> A Binomial(n, p) distribution converges to a Poisson(λ = np) distribution under which condition?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="rl2" id="rl2a"><label class="form-check-label" for="rl2a">When p = 0.5 exactly</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="rl2" id="rl2b"><label class="form-check-label" for="rl2b">When the number of trials n → ∞ while n·p stays constant (equal to λ)</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="rl2" id="rl2c"><label class="form-check-label" for="rl2c">Never — Binomial and Poisson are unrelated</label></div>
    <div id="rl2-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <div class="mb-4">
    <p><strong>Question 3:</strong> In a Q-Q plot comparing quantiles from two distributions, what does it mean when the points fall closely along the diagonal line?</p>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="rl3" id="rl3a"><label class="form-check-label" for="rl3a">The two distributions are unrelated</label></div>
    <div class="form-check"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="rl3" id="rl3b"><label class="form-check-label" for="rl3b">The two distributions are very similar to each other</label></div>
    <div class="form-check mb-2"><input class="form-check-input" type="radio" name="rl3" id="rl3c"><label class="form-check-label" for="rl3c">One distribution has twice the variance of the other</label></div>
    <div id="rl3-feedback" class="mt-1 fw-bold"></div>
  </div>
  <button onclick="checkRelationshipsQuiz()" class="btn btn-primary w-100" style="background-color:#1a4d1a;border:none;font-weight:700;">CHECK ANSWERS</button>
  <div id="relationships-result" class="mt-3 fw-bold text-center"></div>
</div>
